newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's CVRD sets decentralized structure.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CVRD sets decentralized structure.

text.p: Brazil's CVRD is decentralizing its structure just weeks after its privatization, dividing itself into four groups, each with its own autonomous president, the company said Thursday.

Benjamin Steinbruch, CVRD's chairman, said the presidents of the four segments -- corporate center, minerals, aluminium, pulp and paper -- are effectively replacing the post of company president. They will coordinate management within an executive committee that reports to the CVRD board, he said.

"We will have four specialists focusing on their area as if it were the company's only business," Steinbruch told reporters. "This model will allow for greater flexibility as well as greater responsibility in each area."
The model demonstrates that the new controlling shareholders of CVRD are determined to maintain the company's integrity and make each line of business viable and profitable, he said.
The government in early May auctioned off 45 percent of the voting stock of CVRD, or Companhia Vale do Rio Doce.
